definition: A number $\lambda$ such that $A\boldsymbol{v} = \lambda\boldsymbol{v}$ for some non-zero vector $\boldsymbol{v}$, where $A$ is a square matrix; the eigenvalues are the solutions of $\det(A - \lambda I) = 0$.

A non-zero vector $\boldsymbol{v}$ with $A\boldsymbol{v} = \lambda\boldsymbol{v}$ for a square matrix $A$ and some number $\lambda$, so the matrix only stretches, shrinks or flips it; any non-zero multiple of it is also an eigenvector for the same $\lambda$, and the zero vector never counts.
For a $2 \times 2$ matrix $A$, the quadratic $\det(A - \lambda I)$ in $\lambda$, whose roots are the eigenvalues of $A$.

Writing a square matrix as $M = PDP^{-1}$, with eigenvectors of $M$ as the columns of $P$ and the matching eigenvalues, in the same order, on the diagonal of $D$ (zeros elsewhere), so that $M^{n} = PD^{n}P^{-1}$; in IB AI it is done only for $2 \times 2$ matrices with two different real eigenvalues.
